This method first enhances the correlation between feature space and sample space through contrastive learning, effectively addressing the challenge of imbalanced aerial target datasets. Subsequently, a hierarchical variable-length Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model is employed to extract and process information across different time scales, leading to a more comprehensive and accurate understanding of target behavior. Experimental results indicate that our method demonstrates significantly superior performance in complex air combat environments. It notably enhances recognition stability, accuracy, and speed, showcasing strong potential for practical applications.

articleTitle: Overview of Tool Wear Condition Monitoring Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: Tool wear condition monitoring is one of the most important technologies for making machining more efficient and making sure the standard of machining. Finding tool wear accurately is a key part of making machining more efficient, making sure the quality of the object, and extending the life of machine tools. This article talks about how study into tool wear detection technology has grown over the last few years and looks at the main technical connections, like how to get detection signals, extract features, and recognise patterns. This paper talks about intelligent detection technology, which uses neural networks, support vector machines, random forests, and other methods to sort and guess the state of tool wear. In order to show what problems there are with tool wear monitoring technology right now and what the future holds, predictions are given.

articleTitle: Motion Intent Recognition Algorithm for Lower Limb Rehabilitation Robots Based on Dual-Physics Sensor Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: Existing motion intent recognition systems in lower limb rehabilitation robots primarily rely on the fusion of multiple sensor features. Such systems capture the motion characteristics of healthy volunteers during specific movements and then process the data using machine learning algorithms to accurately recognize human motion events, such as forward and backward movements. We address the complexity and inaccuracies of current intent recognition systems by synthesizing feedback from rehabilitation physicians and patients and adopting modular design principles to develop an integrated human motion intent recognition system for lower limb rehabilitation robots. The system utilizes dual physical sensors to collect data on the movement characteristics of the patient’s waist, abdomen, and shoulders, which are then classified using the Transformer-LSTM algorithm. The dataset employed for training and testing the algorithm was gathered from a tertiary care hospital, focusing on the movement characteristics of patients with functional hemiplegia of the lower extremities. Clinical trial results demonstrated that the Transformer-LSTM algorithm achieved an average classification accuracy of 97.54% in recognizing human lower limb movement events, compared to 87.48% with the LSTM algorithm. This lower limb rehabilitation robot also significantly enhances patient motivation and comfort during training.

Author Keywords: Human lower limb motion intention recognition

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Talent Analytics: Unveiling Competency Indicators in Live Streamer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: The burgeoning live-streaming industry has become a transformative force in business, prompting a reevaluation of competency requirements for live streamers. However, there is still a lack of studies that focus on the objective assessment of live streamer competency indicators. This study aims to determine the key competencies of live streamers by utilizing machine learning algorithms for topic modeling. We identified seven core competency indicators for live streamers from 8,743 job advertisements from China's leading job search website, Kanzhun Limited. The top three competencies are "Interaction and Adaptability", "Marketing and Planning Skills", and "Talents and Specialties". The results also indicate that large companies prioritize operational and review abilities, while small companies focus on resource development. Moreover, part-time roles value talents and specialties, whereas full-time positions emphasize marketing and planning skills alongside operational and review abilities. This research provides theoretical insights into competency modeling within the live-streaming context and offers practical implications for talent acquisition and development in the industry. The findings suggest that organizations should tailor their recruitment strategies to align with the specific competencies required for different roles and organizational sizes.

articleTitle: Optimization Model for Garbage Image Classification Based on RepVGG
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: The application of deep learning to the classification of garbage images has been demonstrated to significantly enhance the accuracy and efficiency of classification through the extraction of features and the recognition of patterns. However, in environments with limited resources or computational power, traditional models are unable to effectively handle complex trash image classification tasks. Consequently, the deployment of lightweight models in garbage image classification h as g arnered increasing interest. In this paper, the structure of the RepVGG model is optimized by combining depthwise separable convolution. Adapting the convolutional layers of the original trunk structure to training branches and replacing the convolutional kernel of the trunk with a 5 × 5 convolutional kernel results in the trunk and branches being reparameterized to a single 5 × 5 convolutional layer after training. This design enhances the image feature extraction capability at multiple levels. The inference structure retains the simple stacking of the original convolutional and ReLU layers. In this paper, the improved model is named DSC5RepVGG. The experimental results demonstrate that DSC5RepVGG reduces the number of parameters by 60.97% in comparison to RepVGG, reduces the theoretical floating-point computation by 58.22%, and improves the Top-1 accuracy by 1.29% on Kaggle’s Garbage Classification dataset.

articleTitle: Access Control Attribute Mining Model Based on ALBERT-PFN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: In the evolving field of cybersecurity, efficiently managing Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) remains crucial due to complex attribute relationships. This paper introduces the ALBERT-PFN model, a novel access control attribute mining approach that employs deep learning to transform ABAC challenges into joint entity and relationship extraction tasks. The model leverages ALBERT for contextual word embeddings and a Positional Feature Network (PFN) that dynamically interprets relationships between entities, significantly enhancing both the accuracy and automation of attribute mining. Experimental results show that ALBERT-PFN achieves a precision of 88.13%, a recall of 91.80%, and an F1 score of 89.93% in entity recognition, outperforming existing methods. In relationship extraction, it further excels with a precision of 81.55%, a recall of 72.94%, and an F1 score of 77.01%, underscoring its effectiveness in developing dynamic and precise ABAC policies.

articleTitle: A Novel Framework for Real-Time Water Quality Analysis in Agriculture via ANN and Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: Human faces a severe water crisis exacerbated by urbanization, industrialization, and population growth. The country is threatened by depleting water resources, poor storage capacity, poor infrastructure, and climate change impacts on glaciers. Water quality monitoring reveals significant contamination, with a large portion of water sources unsafe for consumption. Improved water management is crucial. Irrigation enhances farmers' overall well-being and provides a reliable income. Increasing agricultural productivity through irrigation is a crucial approach to reducing poverty caused by the poor performance of rain-fed systems. Consequently, the study examines the factors contributing to the underutilization of land available for irrigation. Integration of Remote sensing technique and ANN to evaluate inland water quality by examining its images, collected from USGS and Copernicus data space sites. IBM SPSS Modeler used to train and produce ANNs for predictive analytics. TSS (Total Suspended Solids), algal blooms, and Chlorophyll-a are related but distinct. TSS measures suspended particles in water, algal blooms indicate rapid algae growth due to nutrient excess, and Chlorophyll-a measures algae concentration. High TSS and Chlorophyll-a can result from algal blooms, impacting water quality and clarity.

articleTitle: Equilibrium Analysis of AI Investment in Financial Markets under Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: This paper extends the monotone supermodular games framework to analyze equilibrium outcomes in financial markets involving AI investments. Using Szkup and Trevino’s results, I demonstrate the existence and uniqueness of Bayesian Nash equilibria, where investors allocate resources based on private signals and AI-driven insights. I explore the impact of coordination, open vs. closed AI models, operational risks like cyber disruptions, and the "data reflection" problem. My findings i ndicate that AI investment equilibria minimize private noise, aligning with risk-dominant strategies in global games.

articleTitle: DF-SegDiff: A Diffusion Segmentation Model using a New Distributed Parallel Computing Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: Brain tumours are among the most life-threatening diseases, and automatic segmentation of brain tumours from medical images is crucial for clinicians to identify and quantify tumour regions with high precision. While traditional segmentation models have laid the groundwork, diffusion models have since been developed to better manage complex medical data. However, diffusion models often face challenges related to insufficient parallel computing power and inefficient GPU utilization. To address these issues, we propose the DF-SegDiff model, which includes diffusion segmentation, parallel data processing, a distributed training model, a dynamic balancing parameter and model fusion. This approach significantly reduces training time while achieving an average Dice score of 0.87, with several samples reaching Dice values close to 0.94. By combining BRATS2020 with the Medical Segmentation Decathlon dataset, we also integrated a comprehensive dataset containing 800 training samples and 53 test samples. Evaluation of the model using Dice, IoU, and other relevant metrics demonstrates that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques.

articleTitle: Traffic Sign Small Object Detection Algorithm Combining Multi-feature and Accurate Location
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: In the rapid development of autonomous driving technology, the accurate detection of traffic signs has become an indispensable part. Traffic signs are usually small in size, which leads to low detection accuracy, missed detections, and false detections with general object detection algorithms when capturing small, low-pixel traffic signs. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a traffic sign small object detection algorithm combining multi-feature and accurate location. The algorithm utilizes a Triple Feature Fusion Module (TFF) to fully integrate features of different scales, providing rich shallow details for small-scale object detection; In addition to the original three detection layers, we have added a dedicated layer for detecting small-scale objects in YOLOv8, enhancing the algorithm's capability for small-sized traffic signs; By combining the normalized Gaussian distance (NWD) and CIoU, the loss function is optimized to tackle the problem that CIoU loss is overly sensitive to the position shifts of small-scale objects. Tested on the TT100K2021 and CCTSDB2021 datasets, the results showed that the mAP of our algorithm reached 82.8% and 81.5% respectively, which is an increase of 9.6% and 2.2% compared to the original YOLOv8. It is proved that the proposed algorithm has remarkable performance in traffic sign detection. https://github.com/ShuaiboChen/SmallObjectDetection.git

articleTitle: A Hand Action Recognition Framework Based on Multimodal Foundation Model and Tracking of Skeleton Point Trajectorie
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: Although accurate hand motion recognition was particularly crucial in monitoring modern industrial assembly lines, it still faced challenges, such as high-cost training datasets and poor real-time performance. In this paper, we propose an innovative paradigm for recognizing hand actions on industrial assembly lines, wherein the problem of hand action recognition was transformed into a hand skeletal point trajectory classification problem. This solved the problem of the requirement for a large dataset and poor real-time performance for action recognition on the assembly line. Comprehensive experiments were concluded to demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the method, wherein the accuracy of hand action recognition reached 98.8% with the proposed methods being implemented in real industrial assembly lines of Midea Group.

articleTitle: Sustainable Cultivation Method of College Student Innovation Teams Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: With the rise of innovation and entrepreneurship education, cultivating college student innovation teams has gained significant attention. Traditional methods face challenges such as information silos, dispersed resources, and inadequate personalized guidance, limiting their effectiveness. This paper proposes a novel cultivation method based on a knowledge graph model for these teams. By utilizing knowledge graph technology, we can model and connect team members, required knowledge, and available resources, facilitating knowledge sharing and communication. In-depth analysis of team members' skills and interests allows for personalized guidance and training. We established a comprehensive knowledge graph incorporating business models, professional knowledge, laws, training, and sustainable development. Two college innovation teams were formed, using both knowledge graph-based and traditional methods for comparison. Results from actual innovation projects demonstrate that the knowledge graph-based approach enhances collaboration, promotes knowledge sharing, and improves the teams' innovation capabilities and competitiveness. This method offers a fresh perspective for cultivating college student innovation teams, addressing the limitations of traditional practices.

articleTitle: Robust Control of Lower Extremity Exoskeleton Rehabilitation Robot Based on Nominal Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: This research tackles the issue of controlling joint angle tracking in lower extremity exoskeleton rehabilitation robots by presenting a method known as Robust Control of Lower Extremity Exoskeleton Rehabilitation Robots based on the Nominal Model (RC-LEERR-NM). Initially, the dynamics model for the single-leg swing phase of the exoskeleton was developed using the Lagrange method, followed by a thorough analysis of the exoskeleton’s gait. The dynamics model was then divided into two components: the nominal model and the robust control, which together form the control terms necessary for the effective management of the exoskeleton system. Additionally, an integral-type Lyapunov function was created to demonstrate that the proposed control system ensures global asymptotic stability. The method’s effectiveness was confirmed through simulations and experimental results, which indicated that the RC-LEERRNM method significantly outperforms PID control in terms of dynamic stability and trajectory tracking accuracy, successfully enabling the lower extremity exoskeleton to accurately follow human gait patterns.

articleTitle: A Bagging RAG Public Opinion Analysis and Guidance Tool Driven by Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: In the context of the information explosion, the analysis of online public opinion holds significant importance for maintaining social stability and fostering the healthy development of information dissemination. To enhance the automated analytical capabilities of online public opinion, this paper presents a Bagging Retrieval Augmented Generation (BRAG) method driven by a large language model. This method extracts feature text from a limited number of online public opinion samples using a large language model to build a public opinion analysis knowledge base. Through the bootstrap aggregating method, the feature text is segmented and recombined, selecting appropriate parts to form critical prompt words that assist the large language model in completing public opinion analysis tasks, thus constructing an effective analytical tool for Weibo public opinion. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed method significantly improves the accuracy, recall and f1-score of public opinion analysis.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Object Detection Based On Adaptive Spatial Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: Object detecting in remote sensing images field is utilized for analyze images of the earth's surface to monitor and understand environmental changes, and to support scientific decision-making and resource management. The existing methods do not fully integrate the context information of the scene, which brings about the decline of detection capability, missed detection and false detection. To tackle this challenge, this paper proposes adopts a remote sensing image object detection method with adaptive spatial attention. This method uses multi-scale convolution kernels to extract feature maps of different scales, thus strengthening the model's feature extraction prowess. The spatial attention is utilized to adaptively adjust the receptive field and leverage contextual information, thereby enhancing the recognition capability for small objects. Experiments on the DOTAv1.0, HRSC2016 and VEDAI remote sensing image datasets demonstrate that the proposed method enhances detection accuracy and effectively mitigates issues of missed and false detections. The source code will be available at https://github.com/yyq0828/ASA.

articleTitle: HRAM: Underwater Hierarchical Route Allocation Mechanism Based on Load Balancing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks are widely used in marine resource exploration and military device deployment. However, uneven network load and high node energy consumption severely hinder their practical applications. In this paper, we established a Hierarchical Underwater multi-hop Wireless Sensor Network model (HUWSN), which describes the data transmission process within the network. Based on the model, we proposed an underwater Hierarchical Route Allocation Mechanism (HRAM) aiming to achieve network load balancing. Specifically, the mechanism first utilized a Balanced Routing Selection Algorithm (BRSA) to form the initial network topology, ensuring a balanced distribution of relay tasks among layers. Subsequently, load distribution over network links was balanced by using the Data Allocation Algorithm based on load factor (DAA). Finally, the allocation of the amount of data in routing was optimized by using the Heuristic Route Allocation Optimization Algorithm (HRAOA). The experimental results showed that compared with existing methods, the proposed mechanism effectively reduces total energy consumption of nodes while maintaining a balanced network load.

articleTitle: Research on Factor Graph-based SLAM Localization Algorithm for Multi-source Sensor Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: A multi-sensor tightly coupled localization algorithm based on a factor graph is proposed to address the challenges of low single-sensor localization accuracy and insufficient robustness of mobile robots in outdoor environments. The algorithm incorporates Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) data at the front end for point cloud de-distortion. It utilizes the IMU pre-integration result as the initial position to enhance point cloud alignment accuracy, thereby improving the overall position estimation of the robot. The back end constructs the IMU pre-integration factor, Lidar odometry factor, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) factor, and loop closure detection factor through a factor graph, and outputs the robot’s state information through incremental optimization. Test results on the M2DGR dataset demonstrate that the algorithm significantly enhances localization accuracy and robustness in both closed-loop and open-loop outdoor scenarios.

articleTitle: Shallow Sea Bathymetric Inversion Based on Multispectral Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: The availability of shallow water bathymetry data is crucial for the research of shallow marine areas. Compared to traditional ship sonar and airborne radar, multispectral satellite remote sensing imagery offers the advantages of low cost, large range, and high update frequency. In this work, the bathymetric inversion of Nanliao Fishing Harbor in Hsinchu City was taken as the research object, and IKONOS high-resolution multispectral images were selected as the data source. we constructed single-band, dual-band ratio, and multi-band combinations of the bathymetry inversion model, based on the theory of remote sensing detection of the bathymetry. Finally, this work adopted the regression analysis for the inversion depth and chart bathymetry, and the results were evaluated according to R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, RMSE, MRE, and MAE indicators. The results showed that the blue-green dual-band ratio model and blue-green-red multi-band model inversion demonstrated the best results, with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> above 0.997. This method could quickly obtain the preliminary bathymetric information of shallow waters from multispectral satellite images through the optical properties of seawater for analysis and application in related marine fields.

articleTitle: Research Review of Ship Power Load Forecasting Based on Intelligent Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: Amidst the swift advancements of the global shipping industry and the escalating demand for energy conservation and emission reduction, ship power load forecasting has emerged as a pivotal research domain to guarantee the stable operation of ship power systems. Precise power load forecasting not only optimizes the scheduling and management of ship power systems but also markedly enhances fuel utilization efficiency and mitigates emissions. In recent years, intelligent optimization algorithms, renowned for their notable advantages in addressing complex nonlinear problems, have been increasingly applied to the study of ship power load forecasting. This paper delves into ship power load forecasting methodologies predicated on intelligent optimization algorithms, with a primary focus on the application of genetic algorithms, particle swarm optimization algorithms, and artificial neural networks. These algorithms emulate natural evolution, swarm intelligence, and neural system mechanisms, thereby effectively addressing complex power load forecasting challenges. In conclusion, ship power load forecasting founded on intelligent optimization algorithms holds substantial theoretical significance and extensive application prospects. With the advancement and application of related technologies, the operational efficiency and reliability of ship power systems will be further augmented, thereby furnishing robust support for attaining green shipping and sustainable development.

articleTitle: A Review on Large Model-oriented Advertising Auction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: Under the background of rapid development of artificial intelligence, advertising auction mechanism which as the one of core area is facing unprecedented transformation. This article aims to analyse basic principles and evolution process of advertising auction mechanism deeply and typically focus on the application status and future trend of multi-model information processing technology in this mechanism. Firstly, this essay gives a comprehensive overview of advertising auction mechanism. Then it systematically summarized from multiple dimension such as the advertising auction market model, advertising production and auction mechanism, advertising automatic bidding strategy, auction mechanism platform design and application. This paper aims to give comprehensive theoretical support and practical guidance to theoretical research and practical application of advertising auction mechanism.

articleTitle: Review on Power Grid Fault Prediction and Location Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data (ICCD)
abstract: Power grid faults are a major factor affecting the reliability and safety of power grids. Therefore, accurately predicting and locating these faults is essential for enhancing operational efficiency and ensuring the stability of power supply. This paper reviews the current research advancements and technical applications in the field of power grid fault prediction and location. It begins by examining existing methods and perspectives on fault prediction, followed by an in-depth exploration of recent developments and practical applications in fault location. We analyze the strengths and challenges of various models in data collection, feature extraction, fault classification, and diagnosis, and discuss potential future research directions. This review aims to provide a comprehensive reference for power system engineers and researchers, aiding them in understanding the latest fault prediction technologies to better manage and maintain the stable operation of power networks.
